text: The way for a young man to rise is to improve himself every way he can, never suspecting that anybody wishes to hinder him. Allow me to assure you that suspicion and jealousy never did help any man in any situation. There may sometimes be ungenerous attempts to keep a young man down; and they will succeed, too, if he allows his mind to be diverted from its true channel to brood over the attempted injury.
author: Abraham Lincoln
reference: Speeches and Letters of Abraham Lincoln, 1832-1865
locator: From a Letter to William H. Herndon. Washington, July 10, 1848
